name: Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy Type 1
aliases: Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy Type I

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Electrophysiological studies showing motor axonal neuropathy with normal sensory nerve conduction
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Lack of significant sensory abnormalities on clinical and electrophysiological examination
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with distal HMN type 1 (e.g., HSPB1, GARS)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal motor weakness and atrophy with electrophysiological evidence of motor axonal neuropathy and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory; sensory nerves are typically spared.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness predominantly in lower limbs
searchTerms: weak muscles at lower limb ends

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle atrophy of feet and hands
searchTerms: muscle wasting in hands and feet
shrinking muscles in fingers and toes
loss of muscle bulk in extremities

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or reduced deep tendon reflexes in affected limbs
searchTerms: absent or weak reflexes in affected limbs

common.symptomName: Foot drop due to dorsiflexor weakness
searchTerms: foot drop from weak foot dorsiflexors
muscle cramps in hands and feet

occasional.symptomName: Mild sensory symptoms such as paresthesia (rarely present)

searchTerms: mild stiff joints in fingers or toes
slight joint tightening in hands or feet
difficulty breathing due to weak respiratory muscles
weakness in muscles that help breathing

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic or inflammatory neuropathies
imaging: Muscle MRI may show selective distal muscle atrophy
Nerve ultrasound typically normal or shows mild nerve enlargement
genetic: Pathogenic variants in HSPB1, GARS, BSCL2, or other distal HMN-associated genes
other: Electromyography (EMG) showing chronic denervation and reinnervation in distal muscles
Nerve conduction studies demonstrating reduced motor amplitudes with preserved sensory responses

distinguishingFeatures: Upper motor neuron signs present in ALS

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks to months
references: Orphanet: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type 1 - ORPHA:139518
